### New

- **Hide Lightning Flashes.** Turning on **Hide Lightning Flashes** in Minecraft's Accessibility settings now also turns off the lyrics' flashes: the glow pulse, the crosshair flash, the hat flare, the sky pulse and the World words' white flash when they appear.
- **Distortion Effects.** Minecraft's **Distortion Effects** setting (in Accessibility settings) now also calms the lyrics' motion: at 0 the line pop, the World words' sway, knock and arrival bounce, and the hat's wobble and spin (without a jump when you move the slider) and the spinning record in the top bar and on the **Record card** stay still, and in between they are slower or smaller. At 0 the World words also just fade when they leave (no rising, sinking, blowing away or shrinking), after you die (no falling), when they join a flowing line (no sliding in) and when they make room for each other (no gliding).
- **Demo song.** While the demo song plays, the top bar shows "Demo" next to the song, so you can tell it from your own music. Switching the demo song on now starts it from the top, playing, instead of somewhere in the middle (or still paused from last time). Turning **Demo song** off while the song library is open brings your own songs back instead of keeping the made-up ones.
- **Spanish, Portuguese, German and French.** The settings, song library, top bar, Record card and tour are now in Spanish (Spain and Latin America), Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), German (Germany, Austria and Switzerland) and French (France and Canada), with Minecraft's own names for its menus.
- **Smooth letters for more alphabets.** Russian, Ukrainian and other Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese lyrics use smooth letters of the same weight as the rest of the line instead of small pixel ones.
- **Russian and Ukrainian.** The settings, song library, top bar, Record card and tour are now in Russian and in Ukrainian, each its own translation, with Minecraft's own names for its menus.
- **Force Unicode Font.** Turning **Force Unicode Font** or **Japanese Glyph Variants** on or off (Options, Language) now fits song titles, lyric lines, the top bar and the settings' About text to the new letters at once, instead of leaving them cut or spaced for the old ones.
- **Narrator and keyboard.** The tour, settings and song library are easier to use with the Narrator and the keyboard.
  - The intro tour now reads its page and the chosen look and layout, and the "<" and ">" buttons are called "Previous look" and "Next look"; the keyboard stays on the button you pressed. In the settings, Left, Right and Space no longer change the setting under the mouse before the mouse has moved: the keyboard first lands on the first setting and says it. Ctrl+Tab also says the setting it lands on, a search result that its tab is hiding says "not in use now", times are read as a number of seconds, and **Timing** says which way is late and early.
  - The library now reads out its sign-in card with the button Enter presses (and the sign-in strip above your recently heard songs with its button), says which song is playing now, names each section with its place ("Liked songs, 2 of 3"), says how many results a search found, and tells you its keys once. Closing a playlist (Esc or the "‹ Playlists" button) brings you back to that playlist instead of the top. In the settings, **Reset all** says "Settings reset", the **Timing** hint is read once when you reach the row instead of on every step, and a key pressed on the row under the mouse says what changed without taking the keyboard there.
  - Enter and Esc are now spoken: the "Starting" and "Playing" messages, the name of a playlist when it opens or closes, "Loading", "Nothing found" and "No liked songs yet", how many results a search found, and that a song is a button or a playlist opens with Enter. The grid, shelf and carousel buttons, the recent searches and the **Open Music tab** button can now be reached with the keyboard (press Up from the top row of songs, then Left and Right; Down goes back).
- **Can't read your music player.** If SkyLyrics can't read your music player (or can't reach the internet for Spotify) for 10 seconds, it now tells you with a pop-up, once per game start, and where to look.

### Fixed

- **Arc layout rows.** In the Arc layout, a line on two or more rows no longer has a word of a lower row drawn over a word of the row above, or of a row higher up when the row in between is short (a word or two); the lower row sits a little further down only when it would otherwise touch.
- **Arc layout big words.** In the Arc layout, two big words (or phrases) side by side in the same row no longer overlap; there is a little more room between them, and nothing changes between normal-sized words.
- **Crashes and clashes.** Pressing Left or Right on **Pick a look** while the look is Custom (after changing any look setting) no longer crashes the game: Right picks the first look and Left the last. A rare error in the mod's drawing no longer crashes the game: the part that failed pauses for 5 seconds and the error goes to the log. Fixes a clash with other font mods on Minecraft 1.21.1 and 1.21.4, and a small memory leak when a letter can't be loaded.
- **Updates.** Updates install and are announced correctly in more situations.
  - An update check that gets an answer which stops halfway (a stalled server or proxy) now gives up after a minute instead of waiting forever.
  - Automatic updates now install for players whose Windows user name has letters beyond plain English ones (Hebrew, Cyrillic, accented) or spaces and signs. An update can no longer leave you without SkyLyrics: the old file is only deleted once the new one is in place, and it is put back if the new one can't be. A download that Windows briefly holds is tried again, and old update leftovers are cleaned up.
  - An update that needs a newer Minecraft or Fabric API than you have is no longer installed: the mod tells you what to update instead, and your working version stays. It remembers this, so the same update is not downloaded again on every start until you update Fabric API, Fabric Loader, Minecraft or Java, or a newer release comes out.
  - With a Fabric API that is too old for SkyLyrics, Minecraft now tells you which version to install instead of crashing at start. The 1.21.10 download no longer says it works on 1.21.9, because no Fabric API for 1.21.9 has what it needs. Coming from 0.8.0, which can't check this yet, Minecraft may ask for a newer Fabric API after this update: install the one it names.
  - If the mods folder's path is very long (about 225 characters or more), an update is no longer downloaded again at every start without being installed: SkyLyrics tells you an update is available so you can install it by hand.
  - If the mod's file is linked into the mods folder from somewhere else (Nix or GNU Stow, for example), you were never told about a new version. Now you are told, though it can't install itself there. On Linux and Mac, an update the mod installs keeps the old file's permissions.
  - An update download that stops halfway is now given up after 5 minutes, instead of holding the update for the rest of the session. The unfinished download is removed from your mods folder, and so is one left over from an earlier run.
- **Two games at once.** Two Minecraft games sharing one game folder no longer undo each other.
  - Two Minecraft games open at the same time (sharing one game folder) no longer undo each other's settings or song timings: when one saves, it keeps what the other changed, and shows it too. The song library's **Recently heard** list keeps the songs both games heard. Saving at the same moment no longer breaks the settings file or loses a renewed Spotify sign-in, and when two games renew the Spotify sign-in together, the second one waits a moment for the first one's new sign-in instead of signing you out. On Windows, a second game no longer deletes the first one's album covers. When both games update, neither deletes the new mod file the other just installed (on Windows too), and a backup of yours in the mods folder ending in .old is never touched.
  - On Linux and Mac, two Minecraft copies that share one mods folder and install the same SkyLyrics update at the same moment no longer leave two SkyLyrics files there (the game would refuse to start).
- **Saving settings and files.** Settings and other saved files are written and read more safely.
  - Settings, song timings, the recently heard list and the Spotify sign-in are written all the way to the disk before they replace the old file, so a crash or power cut right after a save can't empty them. A wrongly typed value in the settings file is repaired on the next save instead of piling up backup copies, one bad song timing no longer drops the others, an oversized or damaged recently heard list is set aside with a copy instead of crashing the game, and a damaged or oversized Spotify sign-in file is kept as a copy and noted in the game log instead of signing you out without a trace.
  - Settings, the recently heard list, the Spotify sign-in and saved covers are read and saved even when Windows, an antivirus or OneDrive holds the file for a moment (the mod tries again), and the Windows music reader's helper file is written the same careful way.
  - If SkyLyrics still can't read your settings or recently heard file at start, it leaves the file alone and keeps a damaged copy next to it, instead of saving defaults over your settings. A settings or Spotify sign-in file left half-written when the game was killed is cleaned up the next time the game starts, once it is a day old.
  - If the game is closed by force while saving, the temporary files it leaves for the settings, the recently heard list, the Spotify sign-in, the update memory and the Windows music reader are now removed at a later start once they are a day old, including recently heard ones left by 0.8.0 and earlier.
- **Hand-edited and newer settings files.** A blank or very long recent search in the settings file no longer breaks the song library, and a hand-typed player name like "Spotify-Web" now picks that player. A number written as NaN or Infinity resets that setting to its default instead of its smallest value, and an empty settings file counts as a fresh start. When a newer SkyLyrics (or a newer Minecraft version of the mod sharing the folder) wrote the settings file, an older one no longer wipes the settings it doesn't know when you change a setting. Saved song timings for titles that carry hidden text-direction marks are found again.
- **Right lyrics for the right song.** Songs get the lyrics that belong to them.
  - A song title like "Levels - Skrillex Remix" in a browser is no longer split into a made-up artist and song, and "Song | Official Music Video" is looked up as "Song" (a timing you saved for one of these browser songs has to be set again). The NetEase backup now finds a song whose title has a tag like "(Remastered 2011)". With no song length (browsers, some local files), an exact title wins over "Song (Live)". Full-width letters match plain ones. With the Spotify app on Linux, two songs with the same name, artist and album are told apart. A title with a version tag in brackets, like "Song (2011 Remaster)", is also looked up without it when nothing is found.
  - "Song (Instrumental)", a karaoke, a backing track or an a cappella version no longer gets the lyrics of the sung song, and the other way round.
  - A song with no artist tag (a browser tab, an untagged file) no longer gets another artist's lyrics for a common title like "Intro": it needs a close length, and when two artists fit it shows none. When the lyrics site only has unsynced lyrics, the backup site is asked for synced ones. Saved unsynced lyrics, and lyrics from the backup site, are checked again after a week and replaced when something better exists. One oddly formatted search result no longer breaks the lookup, and titles that differ only by Hindi or Japanese marks are no longer taken for the same song (accents like "Beyoncé" still match).
- **Lyrics files and lookups.** Odd lyrics files and lookups no longer lose lines or fail.
  - Lyrics with an hour in their time stamps, extra digits after the seconds, wide (full-width) brackets, spaces inside the brackets ("[ 00:12.00 ]"), an invisible space at the start of a line or odd hidden characters no longer lose lines or show as boxes.
  - When the lyrics come from the NetEase backup, a song whose words contain "纯音乐" (Chinese for "instrumental") no longer loses them; only NetEase's own "instrumental" placeholder counts.
  - Files that write times with a comma (`[00:10,50]`) load; lines at the very start no longer get squashed together when a file shifts its timing, and an original line and its translation stay together; NetEase's "pure music, please enjoy" note and a plain "Instrumental" count as instrumental; real plain lyrics are used when the timed copy has only time stamps.
  - One enormous line or a huge number of lines is cut down, and very long song names are shortened (saved timings still match).
  - A very long song title, especially one with a bracket left open, no longer makes the lyrics lookup hang.
  - An error for one odd song title no longer switches the lyrics site (LRCLIB) off for two minutes. Only a site that is really down or too busy does, and even then a song the backup site (NetEase) doesn't have is still asked from LRCLIB. When LRCLIB says it is too busy, the mod now waits as long as it asks before asking again, even if it names a time instead of a number of seconds.
- **Quick skips and fast lines.** Quick skips and fast lines show the right song and all their words.
  - After a quick skip, the new song no longer shows the old song's lyrics, album cover or colour. The top bar, the **Record card** and the shooting stars no longer show the last song's line or "finding lyrics" next to the new song's name. A slow lyrics or album cover lookup for the old song no longer holds up the new one. A lookup cut short by a skip also no longer makes the mod use the backup lyrics site (NetEase) for two minutes, and no longer leaves a half-written lyrics file behind. A song also keeps its lyrics and album cover when one step of the song change fails.
  - In World, the last words of a very short line (rap, fast lyrics) now show before the next line takes over, and the words of a short line start as it comes in. In Arc, words not yet shown fade in as a fast line leaves instead of all flashing on at once. In World, a very long word in a **Flowing line** no longer leaves a big gap before it.
- **Spotify sign-in.** Spotify sign-in is steadier.
  - When Spotify says "too many requests" while renewing your sign-in, SkyLyrics waits as long as Spotify asks (up to 5 minutes). If your Spotify app was deleted or reset, you are signed out with a message to check your Client ID instead of staying "Signed in" while nothing works. A program on your PC can't hold up the sign-in page by sending data slowly, and restarting a sign-in no longer shows the old attempt's error or a false "Sign-in timed out".
  - Pasting a different Client ID while a sign-in waits in the browser now cancels that sign-in, instead of ending in a silent sign-out. A broken reply from Spotify (for example a network login page) no longer stops the sign-in or the polling with no message, and a failed sign-in never says "null".
  - Clicking Sign out or Sign in while SkyLyrics is saving a renewed Spotify sign-in no longer freezes the game for a moment on a slow disk.
  - Signing in to another Spotify account now opens your own playlists without restarting the game.
  - On Windows, the copy SkyLyrics keeps of a damaged Spotify sign-in file is now private to you like the sign-in itself. Before, other accounts on the PC could read it (and the sign-in it may still hold) when the game folder is on another drive.
- **Spotify messages and gaps.** Spotify gaps and errors no longer blink the lyrics out or show raw errors.
  - With Spotify, a moment when Spotify says nothing is playing (around an ad, a track change or a switch to another device) no longer makes the lyrics blink out and come back up to 4 seconds late: the mod asks again after a second. With Spotify signed in, an ad is no longer taken for a song. A Spotify answer without a play state no longer causes an error.
  - When one Spotify song follows another with the same title and artist (like two "Interlude"s), the mod now sees a new song: it looks up the second one's lyrics and starts them from the top instead of carrying on with the first one's. The two still share their per-song **Timing**.
  - A Spotify app that doesn't know your account now tells you to add it under User Management on the Spotify dashboard, instead of "error 403". If Spotify refuses your sign-in even after the mod renewed it, the mod says "Spotify signed you out, sign in again" instead of "error 401". When Spotify can't be reached, the settings show one steady message saying the internet can't be reached (it used to blink on and off and blame the player), and the log gets one warning instead of one a minute.
  - Signing out of Spotify just as the mod asks it for the song no longer brings the old account's song back for a moment.
  - With Spotify signed in, pressing play, pause, next or previous, or moving the song bar, right after the computer wakes from sleep no longer does nothing: the mod renews the Spotify sign-in and sends the press again.
- **Music players.** A player that doesn't say where it is in the song no longer holds the lyrics on the first line; they keep time from when the song started or resumed. When your settings file comes from another computer, the **Player** button shows the player it names instead of "Auto" (SkyLyrics still follows that player when it is open).
- **Linux music players.** More Linux music players are found and read correctly.
  - When the desktop's message-bus address can't be used (an old address left after logging in again, or a kind the mod can't open), SkyLyrics also tries your user's usual bus before saying it can't reach your music players.
  - Where Linux has no desktop message bus (some containers and launchers), the mod no longer tries to reach it twice a second: it waits longer each time, up to 30 seconds, and still finds a bus that shows up later.
  - When a launcher hides your session from the game, the mod now still finds your music players instead of saying it can't reach them. In a Flatpak (for example the Prism Launcher), when it isn't allowed to talk to music players and none show up, the mod now shows the Flatpak hint instead of just "nothing playing".
  - On Linux, players such as Amberol are now shown by their own name, and songs from the library open in the right player.
  - Clicking the progress bar now also moves the song on Linux music players that don't name their tracks the usual way, or don't name them at all.
  - On Linux, a player that is stopped (not just paused) but still remembers its last song (Rhythmbox, VLC) no longer keeps that song in the bar.
  - On Linux, when your music player shows nothing for a second or two between songs, SkyLyrics no longer jumps to a browser tab and keeps showing its song.
- **Windows music player.** The Windows music player link is steadier.
  - The lyrics no longer stand still until the player's next update when Windows has only just started.
  - A player that resumes no longer makes the lyrics skip ahead and back, and one that never says when it updated no longer freezes the lyrics. An album cover that stalls no longer makes the link to your music player time out and restart, and a player that is slow to answer once no longer makes the lyrics blink away. An album cover that was still the last song's is read again a few seconds later. Pause, Skip and Seek no longer reach another app when the one you follow has closed. Changing the computer's clock, or the clock jumping after sleep, no longer makes the lyrics freeze or jump to the end of the song.
- **Mac music player.** On a Mac, lyrics no longer run a little late, and a song with something missing (for example a local file or podcast with no album cover) still shows its title and lyrics. On a Mac, a Spotify ad is no longer looked up as a song, and two songs with the same title, artist and album are told apart. Music's internet radio now shows the playing song instead of the station name.
- **Album covers.** Album covers show, download and reload more reliably.
  - An album cover shows even when it can't be saved for next time, and a damaged saved album cover is fetched again. One that couldn't download (no network, a slow or busy server, a Wi-Fi sign-in page) is tried again every few seconds to a minute for about half an hour, instead of staying missing until the next song. One that downloads but can't be read (an unusual colour format or a cut-off file) is given up on instead of being downloaded again every few minutes, and a transparent cover no longer tints the lyrics with a colour hidden under its see-through parts. One that stalls while downloading is cut off instead of blocking the next song's album cover. An album cover the game can't read, or a song with the same name as an earlier one but another album cover, no longer keeps the earlier song's colour.
  - On Linux, a player that gives its album cover as a file with spaces or accents in the name, or in another odd file-address form, now shows it. On Windows, an album cover that the player gives as a web-style file address (starting with file://) shows too.
  - A cover that the player corrects a few seconds into a song (the first one was the last song's, for example on YouTube in Edge or Chrome) now replaces the wrong one on screen. A Windows PC that blocks the music reader no longer has it retried every 15 seconds all session: the waits grow up to 5 minutes and the warning is logged once. The recently heard list no longer remembers a Windows cover's temporary file.
  - The last song's album cover no longer shows for a moment next to the new song's title.
- **Song library.** Lists, searches, messages, names and buttons in the song library work more reliably.
  - Songs in a long list show up right away as you scroll, and can't be clicked before they appear. If more of a list fails to load, the library tries again a few times by itself; in the grid view you can also click the error line. Spotify playlists with local files or podcasts no longer repeat songs or stop loading partway. Scrolling the recently heard list can no longer cause an error. Pressing Space on a playlist opens it without jumping to search. Pressing Enter after changing the search no longer plays a song from the old results. Play no longer waits behind searches (a busy Spotify could leave it doing nothing for up to 30 seconds), searches you typed past are dropped, old results can't be picked while you are still typing, a double-click on a playlist no longer plays a song from it, the local Spotify app is tried even when Spotify can't list your devices, and a long "Nothing found" text is cut to fit.
  - A song no longer shows twice in Liked songs or Recently heard when the list changes while you scroll, and Recently heard search finds "Beyoncé" when you type "beyonce". When Spotify is busy for a long time, the library says so at once instead of loading for half a minute, and if **Play** can't reach Spotify it says why (signed out or offline). An empty or garbled answer from Spotify (a Wi-Fi login page, say) shows "Spotify didn't answer" instead of an end to the list. If Spotify has blocked the mod's app for your account, the library now says to add your account under User Management instead of asking you to sign in again. A song that Spotify refuses for another reason than a missing Premium no longer says Premium is needed. With nothing playing, a song starts on your computer first instead of whichever device Spotify lists first. Your own playlists open even when Spotify didn't say who you are.
  - Closing the song library while Spotify asks SkyLyrics to wait no longer leaves the next list you open stuck on loading for up to 30 seconds.
  - Your Spotify playlists no longer show one playlist twice, or stop loading partway, when Spotify leaves a gap in the list (a playlist it won't show the mod).
  - Song, playlist, album and artist names from your Spotify library and from Recently heard are cleaned like the song playing now: hidden text-direction marks and stray tabs no longer flip or box them, and very long names are cut. A song title made only of invisible characters is treated like a song with no title. Lyrics containing a broken emoji character are saved again instead of being fetched anew on every play.
  - The short messages in the song library ("Playing …", errors) stay up as long as Minecraft's **Notification Display Time** says, like Minecraft's own pop-ups.
  - On a small window or a large GUI scale, the strip above your recently heard songs ("Sign in to Spotify on the Music tab…", with its **Open Music tab** button) now wraps onto a second line when its text doesn't fit, instead of cutting it off; in Spanish, Portuguese and Hebrew its text and button are also shorter.
  - The song library's Spotify sign-in buttons, **Done** and **Try again** grow to fit their text, so Spanish, Portuguese and Hebrew words no longer run out of them or overlap; when the sign-in card is too narrow, its buttons go one above the other.
  - In the grid view, when more of a long list fails to load, its message and the click that tries again now show under the last row. Before, they sat just below the bottom of the scroll, so the list seemed to end there.
  - In the grid view, holding Down in a column that the half-full last row doesn't reach no longer stops there for good: the next page of songs now loads, so Down carries on. Before, the list seemed to end after about 48 songs unless you scrolled with the mouse.
  - After you sign in to Spotify (or switch Demo song) from the **Open Music tab** button above your recently heard songs, the new list starts at its first song. Before, the card you had chosen in the old list stayed chosen by its place, so the carousel could open in the middle of your liked songs, and with fewer liked songs than that place the arrow keys and Enter did nothing.
  - In the shelf view, when more of a long list fails to load, its message now shows after the last column, and a click on it tries again (the library also still tries a few times by itself). Before, nothing showed and the list just seemed to end. "Loading…" at the end of the shelf also shows whole instead of cut to its first letters.
- **Keys.** Keys in the song library and settings behave as expected.
  - A letter key used for the song library (N) no longer closes the library while you type a search (Esc, or Ctrl, or Cmd on a Mac, with that key, closes it), also on Minecraft 26.3, where Ctrl+C and Ctrl+X in the library search work now too. Holding play/pause, next, previous or the lyrics toggle acts once instead of repeating, holding the settings or library key no longer makes the screen flicker, and Shift+Down in the settings moves down. Holding the library key right after it opens no longer fills the search with letters. In the library search, Ctrl+C copies and Ctrl+X cuts the text, and Ctrl+V pastes from anywhere in the library, with line breaks and odd characters cleaned out.
  - On keyboards that type letters with AltGr (Polish, Czech, and others) or Option on a Mac, those letters now type in the song library and the settings search instead of closing the library or copying or cutting the search text.
  - With Iris installed, an **Open song library** key you set to K (the same key as Iris's shader switch) is moved back to N only once, not on every start.
- **Mac keys.** On a Mac, Cmd+Page Up and Cmd+Page Down switch the settings tabs (on Minecraft 1.21.11 and newer only Ctrl did), and Cmd with the library key closes the song library, like Ctrl. Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Page Up/Down switch the settings tabs, and Ctrl with the song library key closes the library, as on the other versions (Cmd works too).
- **Clicks and sliders.** Clicks and slider drags work as they should, including on Minecraft 26.3.
  - In the settings and the song library, a left click on the mod's own tabs, buttons and sliders now works at once on Minecraft 26.3, where the game numbers the mouse buttons differently; before, it came a few frames late and a very quick click was missed. A slider or scroll bar grabbed by such a late click is also let go again when you release the button. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+X and Ctrl+F in the mod's screens follow the letter of your keyboard layout there (Dvorak, Colemak, AZERTY), not the QWERTY key position.
  - On Minecraft 26.3, a click outside the game window no longer counts as a click inside it.
  - In the settings, letting go of the right or middle mouse button while you drag a slider or the scroll bar with the left no longer drops the drag.
- **Settings scroll.** **Open Music tab** in the song library now takes you down to the Spotify card every time. Settings tabs also keep their place after you visit a shorter tab.
- **Reset all and Done.** In a small window or at a big GUI scale, the "Click again to reset" button of the longer languages (Russian, Ukrainian, Spanish, Portuguese and others) no longer runs under **Done**, where a click on **Done** reset every setting. Its words are cut to fit instead.
- **Settings search letters.** The settings search finds a word however your keyboard types its letters: any apostrophe (' ’ ʼ) finds the others, so the Ukrainian **Сузір’я** and **М’які краї** are found as typed, ß and ss find each other (**Grösse** finds **Größe**, also from a Swiss keyboard, which has no ß) and oe finds œ (**coeur**). The song library's search of your recently heard songs matches the same way.
- **Preview hint.** In a small window or at a big GUI scale, the hint shown while you preview (or that nothing is playing) now wraps onto more lines instead of running off both sides of the screen, which it did in English too.
- **Finding a look.** The settings search now finds **Pick a look** by the name of any look, as your game shows it or in English ("Dreamy", "Verträumt", "Грёзы"), instead of saying nothing matches.
- **Setting tooltips.** The tooltip that shows a setting's cut-off description now wraps onto several lines and stays inside the screen at both sides, instead of one long line running off the right edge (long German and Russian ones did, most of all in a small window). In Hebrew its lines read right to left.
- **World words.** World words stay put and behave better around moves, respawns and each other.
  - On Linux, a music player that answers slowly, or Spotify right after a pause or resume, no longer makes the World words vanish for a moment. Moving the **Timing** slider no longer makes them blink.
  - In the World layout the song title shows for its full time even when the lyrics take a moment to load, and a long title is shrunk to fit.
  - Respawning or changing world during the end of a line no longer flashes its last words, and a word more than 48 blocks away fades out instead of vanishing. Swinging your arm while the World lyrics are hidden no longer knocks a word when they show again.
  - In the World layout, two words that overlap by a sliver side by side now part sideways instead of sliding into each other and jittering or stacking.
  - In the World layout, the words now travel with you when you move very fast (a long fall, a hard knock) and, with **Elytra mode** on, when you launch with a Riptide trident, instead of being left behind and replaced by new ones. Teleporting still leaves them where they were.
- **Long lines.** Very long lines no longer freeze, stutter or write over themselves.
  - A very long line, such as plain lyrics that arrive as one line or a long Chinese or Japanese line, no longer freezes or slows the game in the Arc layout or makes it stutter in the World layout. In the Arc layout such a line now scrolls so the words being sung stay in front of you (before, they could be above the view and the sky looked empty).
  - With **Flowing line** on, a long line that runs down into a hillside or fills the sky no longer writes over its own earlier words: it starts over at the top, and its old words fade out at once. In a tunnel or right by a wall it carries on as before.
  - With **Flowing line** on, a long line starts over at the top when its next row would run off the bottom of the screen (it follows where you look and your field of view, keeps clear of the hotbar, and allows for the ends of a row sitting lower on screen), and when you look steeply down (bridging, digging down) the line now starts a little above where you look instead of out of view.
  - With **Flowing line** on and a fixed **Direction** (North, East, South or West) or the **View lock**, a long line no longer starts over one row at a time when you look away from it.
  - With **Flowing line** on, a long line no longer starts again on top of its own first words at bigger sizes or when you look straight up or down, and a very long line starts over higher up instead of running below your feet. The words are also laid out again when you change the font.
  - With **Flowing line** on, two words of a row are no longer drawn over each other on rows that sit high or low in the sky; those words now get room for the extra width they take there.
  - With **Flowing line** on, a phrase in the other reading direction (an English phrase in a Hebrew line, or a Hebrew phrase in an English line) no longer runs into the word next to it on rows high or low in the sky.
  - With **Flowing line** on, Hebrew and Arabic words on a slanted row no longer touch their neighbours near the top of the screen.
  - With **Flowing line** on, a phrase in the other reading direction (an English phrase in a Hebrew line, or a Hebrew phrase in an English line) now stays on its line's rows: its words no longer jump to the far side of the middle of the screen, and a phrase too long for one row goes on at the start of the next row instead of running off the side of the screen.
  - With **Flowing line** and **Elytra mode** on, a phrase in the other reading direction (an English phrase in a Hebrew line, or a Hebrew phrase in an English line) now stays together when you turn while it is being written, instead of its last words landing away from its first ones.
- **Rejoining a world.** With the Arc layout, rejoining a world (or joining another one) no longer leaves the lyric line off to the side for a moment, where you were looking in the last world, and **Hide in caves** and **Show underground** ask the new world at once instead of using the last world's answer.
- **Sky effects fading in and out.** Sky effects fade smoothly instead of cutting in or popping.
  - The sky effects now fade in and out smoothly when the time of day jumps (/time set, or a server skipping the night) instead of cutting in a single frame. Changing **Night sky** while it is night fades the old sky out before the new one comes in. With **Pulse with the lyrics** on and no synced lyrics showing (unsynced lyrics, no lyrics, an instrumental song, or lyrics hidden), the sky is no longer a little dimmer than with it off. The sparkles no longer drift in from a stale spot when they come back. On 1.21.11 and newer, in light rain the sky effects are no longer dimmer than they should be. They also fade out while a boss bar pulls the fog in (some servers' boss bars do), like the vanilla sky.
  - The sky fades back in after leaving the Nether or the End, or coming up out of water, instead of popping in. It fades out under Blindness and Darkness, as the vanilla sky does. The Comet sky no longer flickers on 26.2 and later.
  - Joining a world right after leaving one at night no longer flashes the old night sky for half a second.
  - With the game's clock frozen (`/tick freeze`), `/time set day` or `night` now changes the painted sky and the lyrics' daylight at once instead of when you next move. This also holds for the first `/time set` after freezing, which could leave the sky on the old time of day (an aurora in daylight) until the next change. Sparkles and shooting stars start fresh after the sky has been hidden instead of gliding in from where they were, and sky animations stay smooth in very long sessions.
- **Sky effects.** Sky effects follow your view and look right in more situations.
  - With **Lazy follow** on or off, the sparkles and shooting stars now follow your view the same way the lyrics do, and they change line at the same moment as the words. They stay visible in front of the eclipse. With the World layout, the sparkles stay with the words even when **Lazy follow** was left on from another layout.
  - Joining another world no longer keeps the old world's anchor, so the lyrics and sky effects start where you look. A word blown away by the Blow leave no longer vanishes early near the edge of the view.
  - On 1.21.11 and newer, rain at night no longer makes the lyrics take daytime colours and a dark edge; clear weather looks as before at every time of day.
  - The thin lines of the painted skies (Synthwave, Moonlight) and the constellations keep their width while you zoom with a spyglass, and with Speed or sprinting, instead of getting about 11 times too thick when zoomed.
  - With **Glow with the lyrics** off, the propeller cap turns at its calm speed.
- **Bars and Record card.** The top bar, bottom bar and Record card keep clear of other things on screen.
  - The top bar, and the **Record card** in a top corner, hide while the debug screen (F3) is showing. They also fade to black with the rest of the screen when you sleep, instead of staying bright over it. A top bar on a medium-wide screen moves down below the potion effect icons when its numbers would reach them, and the **Record card** in a top corner moves below the boss bars on a narrow screen. A **Record card** in a top corner with the top bar at the top no longer sits on top of the bar on a small window or a big GUI scale: it moves down below it. A song title that fits no longer ends with a lone "…" where the artist would be. A **Record card** in the bottom left corner also hides under F3 when it stands tall enough to reach the debug text (on a small window or a big GUI scale), and a player that reports an absurd song length (over a day) gets no progress bar instead of garbled times.
  - The bottom bar sits above the held item's name, above the hearts and armour when you have several rows of them, and above the text that a jukebox or a command shows over the hotbar. A bigger **Bar size** grows upward instead of off the screen. On a narrow screen a big **Bar size** now fits: the bar shrinks and, if needed, hides the stats and then the clock. The **Record card** in a bottom corner now sits above the bar instead of covering it, and above the armour and the held item's name.
  - Holding Tab on a server no longer draws the player list over the top bar or a **Record card** in a top corner: they fade out while it shows and back when you let go. A bottom bar no longer lifts when a server sends an empty action bar message to clear it.
  - A **Record card** on the right steps above or below the scoreboard sidebar, or fades when there is no room. In the bottom right it moves up above the subtitles only while some show, all of them at once. While the chat is open, both bottom cards sit above its text box, and in the bottom left the card fades where the chat covers it (not when chat is set to Hidden). In Minecraft's demo version, the top bar, the card and the potion effect icons leave room for the demo timer.
  - A word wider than the top bar (a web address, a long compound word, a line of one long word) now shows its start while it is sung instead of jumping to its end.
  - A see-through top bar, album cover circle or progress bar no longer shows a faint darker line through its rounded ends at some sizes.
- **Intro tour.** The first-run tour's look page now starts on your current look (or says Custom) instead of Neon, and the next and previous buttons step from it. The intro tour fits small windows and big GUI scales. It no longer opens over a screen that replaced the title screen, and its last page says the keys work in a world. The "Where the songs come from" text no longer runs under the Demo song button in longer languages or on a Mac (a cut line ends in "…"), and the keyboard stays on a sensible button when you change pages or resize the window.
- **Title screen lyrics.** In a tall, narrow window they're sized to fit the width instead of running off both sides. A button another mod puts in a bottom corner no longer pushes them down until they vanish; they stay under the menu buttons and keep clear of it.
- **Right-to-left lyrics.** Lyrics with hidden direction marks or mixed directions read correctly.
  - A lyric line carrying hidden text-direction codes (copied from some websites) no longer shows reversed. Right-to-left lyrics (Hebrew, Arabic) look as before.
  - In the Arc layout, and in World with **Flowing line** on, a Hebrew or Arabic line with an English phrase in it (or an English line with a Hebrew phrase) now reads each part in its own direction, so "NYC 2024" no longer comes out as "2024 NYC". In World, a line that starts over in the middle of such a phrase keeps the rest of the phrase in order. Quotes and signs like « » ‹ › ≤ ≥ now turn the right way in Hebrew and Arabic text, and Arabic words in the Arc layout are spaced to fit.
  - Hebrew and Arabic titles that carry invisible left-to-right or right-to-left marks no longer draw boxes or miss their lyrics, and lyric lines that carry such marks no longer draw them as boxes in the sky, the top bar or the **Record card**: the marks still set the word order.
- **Hebrew and Arabic settings and numbers.** Hebrew and Arabic text and numbers in settings and cards read the right way round.
  - With the game in Hebrew, lines in the settings, the intro tour and the song library that start with an English word ("Beli's SkyLyrics…", "NetEase Cloud Music…") now read right to left like the rest of their paragraph, and so does the settings footer ("J או Esc לסגירה").
  - In a Hebrew game, an English word now finds every setting it names, also where two English words share one Hebrew word (Position and Placement, Words and Lyrics, Arc and Rainbow). Search ignores accents, Hebrew vowel marks and final letter forms, and the invisible marks and odd spaces that pasted text can carry. With the Narrator on, it says how many settings were found. Long result headings are cut to fit the window.
  - With the game in Hebrew or Arabic, the **Record card**'s time left reads "-2:35" instead of "2:35-", and the **Height**, **Distance** and **Size** sliders read the right way round ("-10°", "0.50×"). In every language, the time left at the end of a song reads "0:00", not "-0:00".
- **Minecraft 1.21.1 to 1.21.5.** On 1.21.1 the top bar's text is clipped right at every **Bar size**, and the lyrics, bar and card no longer cover the chat. On 1.21.1 to 1.21.5, setting descriptions are no longer cut off at the edge of the list. A very faint glow (the previous and next lines, the end of the pulse) no longer flashes as solid colour. The settings and the song library, opened from the title screen, show the menu background instead of black.
- **Caves and the Nether.** **Show underground too** now also works in the Nether (when **See through blocks** is off). Swimming deep underwater no longer counts as being in a cave.
- **Elytra mode.** After a steep dive or climb, the words come back to where they were once you level out, instead of staying higher or lower.
- **Lyrics stuck in the wrong place.** In a rare case where the game gave a broken camera position, the lyrics could stay pinned in the wrong place or the **View lock** could stick. They now recover.
- **Effects after loading.** With **Effects** on Auto, reloading resources or switching shaders no longer leaves the lyrics on Light effects for up to two minutes, and a single stutter no longer counts as a slow game (stutter that keeps coming still does).
- **No odd formatting from song text.** A song title, artist, album or lyric line that contains a section sign (§) followed by a letter no longer turns the text coloured, bold or flickering in the sky, the top bar or the song library; the sign and its letter are left out.
- **Safer downloads and caches.** Downloads are safer and the cache folders stay small.
  - An album cover address that points at a shared folder on another computer is no longer opened (on Windows that could have sent your login details to that computer). An album cover link from the internet can no longer redirect the game to this computer or your home network. Links your music player gives directly still work, so album covers from a music server on your own network keep showing. Replies from the lyrics sites are limited in size and time. A lyrics file with a long run of odd characters can no longer slow the lyrics down. Odd data from the NetEase backup no longer makes a song's lyrics search fail for good.
  - Saved lyrics and album covers are kept to their limits while you play, not only when the game starts, so a very long session or skipping through thousands of songs no longer lets the folders grow far past them.
- **Hebrew and Arabic artists in the top bar.** When the top bar shows the song's name and a Hebrew or Arabic artist, the dot between them now sits between the name and the artist, instead of after the artist with the artist run straight into the name (the same for an artist written in digits only, like "112", in a Hebrew or Arabic game). A shortened artist keeps its "…" at the end it is read to.
- **Top bar note without a cover.** On Minecraft 1.21.1 to 1.21.5, the note the top bar shows when a song has no album cover no longer blinks bright white for a moment as the bar appears or hides.
- **Choices in a small window.** In the smallest window (a 640x480 window at GUI scale 2, for example), a choice whose names don't fit side by side even on a line of their own now shows the picked name between two arrows, like **Night sky**, instead of running off the row's left edge, where its first choices were cut away and couldn't be clicked (in English the Look tab's **Colour** lost "Album" and **Font** lost the start of "Smooth"; in Russian **Font** too).
- **Sliders in a small window.** In a small window or at a big GUI scale, where a slider sits on a line under its name, a click on its name or description no longer grabs the slider and changes the setting; only the slider's own line does.
- **Status line.** The Music tab's **Status** (and the other read-only lines, like **Right now**) now uses all the room beside its name instead of stopping at a fixed width, so a long one is no longer cut short (in Spanish, "Reproduciendo la canción de prueba" showed as "Reproduciendo la canción de…").
- **Tour arrows.** With the game in a right-to-left language, the "<" and ">" buttons on the tour's **Pick a look** page now point outwards (the previous look on the left, the next on the right) instead of both pointing in at the look's name.
- **Tour on a Mac.** On a Mac, the tour's **Where the songs come from** page no longer cuts its text off with "…" in some languages, leaving out the line about the demo song: those texts are a little shorter, so every word fits above the **Demo song** button.
- **Cut-off names and values.** A setting whose name ends in "…", and a read-only line cut short like the **Status**, now shows its whole text in a tooltip when you point at it, as a cut-off description already did. In the smallest window that happens to the Russian **Song name only on change** (Display tab), the German **Flash with the lyrics** (Look tab, with a crosshair picked) and the Spanish **Status** while the demo song plays.
- **Links on the About tab.** After you click **LRCLIB**, the keyboard is on it: Enter opens LRCLIB again and the Narrator says "LRCLIB, 2 of 2", instead of Enter opening GitHub.
- **Record card and the scoreboard.** In a small window or at a big GUI scale, a **Record card** on the right that steps out of the way of a server's scoreboard sidebar no longer drops down over the hunger bar, the XP bar or the held item's name. It goes above the sidebar when there is room there, and fades while there is none.
- **Record card under the open chat.** In a small window or at a big GUI scale, the open chat's messages are no longer drawn over a **Record card** in the bottom right or in a top corner: the card fades while the chat's box covers it, as it already did in the bottom left (not when chat is set to Hidden). The box is only as tall as the chat's lines, so a chat with a few lines at the bottom leaves a top card in place, and an empty one leaves every card.
- **Record card and top bar when the music stops.** When the music stops, the **Record card** and the top bar keep showing the last song (its name, artist, times and lyric line) while they fade out, instead of showing "Unknown song" for a moment.
- **Record card and many potion effects.** A **Record card** in the top left now moves down under the potion effect icons when there are enough of them for their row to reach it (in a small window or at a big GUI scale, from about seven effects), as a card in the top right already did, instead of overlapping them.
- **Hats on a mob head or player head.** With a mob head or player head on, the hats now sit on top of it the way they sit on your bare head. Before, its corners stuck up through the brim of the **Top hat** and the edge of the **Propeller cap**, and a player head hid the **Flower crown**'s vine and leaves: the hats grew only as much as for a helmet, and Minecraft draws a worn head bigger than a helmet.
- **Lines layout after the last lyric.** Once a song's last line has been over for a second and a half and fades out, the line above it (the previous line) now fades with it, instead of staying in the sky through the whole outro. The same goes for the notes of a closing pause (lyrics that end with an empty line) and the last words above them.
- **Big lyrics stay on the screen.** From a **Size** of about 1.8 at the usual FOV (sooner with a lower FOV or a squarer window), a long line in the Lines layout could run off both sides of the screen, its first and last words out of sight. Now its rows are wrapped narrow enough to fit across the screen; at the usual sizes nothing changes.
- **The first line in the Lines layout.** In a song whose singing starts within the first two and a half seconds (the demo song too), the first line no longer waits in the middle, where the line being sung goes. It waits below, like every next line. With the **Rise** animation (the **Karaoke** look) it used to drop a row as it started and then rise back up; now it rises straight from there.
- **Sky pulse at a song change.** With **Pulse with the lyrics** on, the night sky no longer jumps a third brighter at once when the song changes (while the next song's lyrics are found) and back down when they arrive, or when the lyrics hide in a menu with **Hide in menus** on. It now eases between its steady and pulsing brightness over about a second, also when you switch the pulse or **Hide Lightning Flashes**.
- **Turning sky effects off at night.** Turning **Constellations** on or off while they are in view now fades them in or out like the rest of the sky instead of making them pop. Turning off the last sky effect (**Night sky** Off with **Constellations**, **Shooting stars** and **Twinkling stars** off, or **Constellations** off with **Night sky** already Off) now fades the sky out instead of cutting it off at once.
- **Hide in caves and cave water.** With **Hide in caves** on, putting your head under the water of a pool or lake in a dark cave no longer brings the lyrics, the top bar and the **Record card** back until you come up again. Diving in open water still doesn't hide them, and swimming out from under cover into open water, however deep, shows them again before you surface.
- **Hide in menus and F3 + Esc.** With **Hide in menus** on, pausing a single-player game with F3 + Esc (which stops the game without opening the menu) no longer hides the lyrics, since no menu is on the screen. The pause menu (Esc, or the game losing focus) still hides them.
- **Music player pop-up in a small window.** In the smallest window (a 640x480 window at GUI scale 2, for example), the "SkyLyrics can't read your music player" pop-up is no longer wider than the screen in German, French, Russian and Ukrainian, nor is the "can't reach the internet or Spotify" one in those languages and Portuguese. Its left end was cut off by the screen's edge, in Ukrainian with the first few letters of each line. Those texts are a little shorter.
- **Song library tabs in a small window.** In the smallest window, the Spanish and European Portuguese tabs above the songs no longer run under the **Grid**, **Shelf** and **Carousel** buttons, where the end of the **Playlists** tab was hidden and a click on it picked a view instead. The **Liked songs** tab is now called "Canciones favoritas" in Spanish and "Favoritas" in European Portuguese.
- **Song library messages.** The message at the bottom of the song library after you click a song or a playlist now goes onto a second line when it is too long for one, instead of ending in "…". In the smallest window that cut off the made-up songs' "These songs are made up, so nothing plays" in Spanish, French, European Portuguese and Russian, and "Spotify keeps this playlist's songs hidden, so it plays from the top" in every language (in a 1280x720 window at GUI scale 3 too, in German, Spanish, French, Portuguese and Russian).
- **Song counts under playlists.** In the song library's grid, a playlist's song count that is too long for its card no longer ends in "…": it shows the number after a note instead, like "♪ 13". In the smallest window that cut the made-up playlists of 10, 13 and 14 songs in Spanish ("13 canciones"); in a 1280x720 window at GUI scale 3 every made-up playlist in Spanish and French, playlists of 100 songs or more in Portuguese, and of 1000 or more in English, German and Russian.
- **Why the song library didn't load.** When the song library can't load your songs, the reason now goes onto a second or third line instead of ending in "…". "Spotify blocked this app. On the Spotify dashboard, add your account under User Management" was cut off in every language, in the smallest window and in a 1280x720 window at GUI scale 3 alike; in the smallest window it now takes three lines in German, French, Russian and Ukrainian. "Sign out and sign in again on the Music tab to use the song library" and "Spotify no longer accepts your Client ID, check it and sign in again" were cut off too. The same goes for a later page that fails as you scroll, under the grid or after the shelf's last column, and a click on any of its lines still tries again.
- **Spotify sign-in strip in Russian and Ukrainian.** In the smallest window, the strip above the songs you heard lately that asks you to sign in to Spotify no longer ends its second line in "…" in Russian and Ukrainian, and neither does the Russian one that asks you to sign in again. Those texts are a little shorter: like the German, Spanish, French and Portuguese ones, they leave the Music tab to the button beside them.
- **Real lyrics over an empty copy.** When the lyrics site (LRCLIB) has several copies of a song and one of them holds only time stamps, only tags or words without times, that copy no longer wins over one with real timed words just because its length is a little closer. Before, such a song could show "instrumental" for good, or no lyrics, although its lyrics were there.
- **Backup lyrics for a song with no artist.** A song with no artist tag (a browser tab, an untagged file) whose title two artists share at about the same length no longer gets one of their lyrics from the backup site (NetEase). It now shows none, as the main site already did.
- **Artists whose name starts with "&".** An artist whose name starts with "&" no longer gets another band's lyrics for a song of the same name. Cutting a credit like "A, B" down to its first artist used to leave such a name empty, and the lookup then searched by the title alone.
- **Pausing a player that doesn't say where the song is.** Some music players and websites never tell where in the song they are, so the lyrics follow the clock from when the song started. Pausing one of them no longer sends the lyrics back to the first line, and playing it again goes on from where you paused instead of starting the lyrics over.
- **Pausing on Windows.** On Windows, pausing a player that never says when it last told where the song is (some browser tabs and players) no longer sends the lyrics back to the start of the song, or to the last spot it told, and playing it again goes on from where you paused.
- **A late cover from a player that doesn't say where the song is.** When such a player sends the song's cover, length or artist a moment after its title, as browsers often do, the lyrics no longer start counting again from that moment, so they no longer run late for the rest of the song or go back to the first line.
- **Holding the now-playing or lock key.** Holding the **Show now-playing card** or **Lock lyrics here** key a moment too long no longer flips it on and off many times a second, leaving it either way: like the show/hide lyrics and music keys, it now acts once per press. The **Lyrics are late** and **Lyrics are early** keys still keep stepping while held.
- **Closing the settings or song library with its key.** Closing the settings with J (or the song library with Ctrl+N) and holding the key a moment too long no longer opens them again right away: the key has to be let go and pressed again.
- **The lock key with Floating lyrics.** With **Placement** on **Floating** (Arc or Lines), where nothing can be pinned, the **Lock lyrics here** key no longer says "Lyrics locked here" and quietly turns on **View lock**: it says only lyrics in the sky can be locked and changes nothing. With **Direction** on N, E, S or W, unlocking now says "Lyrics unlocked" instead of "Lyrics follow again", since the lyrics go back to that side of the sky.
- **Twinkling stars in the World layout.** In the World layout with **Direction** on N, E, S or W, the **Twinkling stars** now stay round the words on that side of the sky instead of following your view when **Placement** was left on **Floating** from another layout (Placement is hidden in World).
- **An unbound settings or library key.** With **Open settings** or **Open song library** set to no key in Controls, the game log no longer fills with "Invalid key" errors (about 60 lines a second for each such key) on Minecraft 1.21.1 to 26.2.
- **Crosshair and hat flicker with no new line.** With **Flash with the lyrics** (a crosshair picked) or the hat's **Glow with the lyrics** on, the crosshair and the hat no longer brighten faintly for a moment when a song's lyrics first come up, or at each new line while the lyrics are hidden (switched off, or by **Hide in menus** or **Hide in caves**). It was the fading end of a flash that never started; real new lines flash as before.
- **Type animation and fast lines.** With the **Type** animation (Lines layout), a line sung faster than it types (a fast rap line, or a long one on two rows) now keeps up with the singing: the **Karaoke fill** no longer runs on into letters that aren't typed yet, and the end of the line shows before the next line takes over (with **Previous line** off it never showed at all). Seeking into the middle of a line shows what has been sung at once and types on from there.
- **Attack meter under a picked crosshair (1.21.1).** On Minecraft 1.21.1, with a crosshair style picked, the attack meter under it is see-through and inverted like the game's own again, instead of a solid grey and white bar.
- **Spotify after the computer sleeps.** With Spotify signed in, when Spotify asks for a renewed sign-in in the middle of a song (as it can after the computer wakes from sleep), the lyrics no longer run ahead of the song by up to half the time the renewal took. Before, when that was under about a third of a second, they stayed that far ahead until the next pause, skip or seek.
- **Big Arc lyrics stay on the screen.** In the Arc layout with a big **Size** (sooner with a lower FOV or a squarer window, such as one tiled to half the screen), the rows of a long line could run off the left and right sides of the screen, their first or last words out of sight: in a square window at Size 3, for one. Now such a line is cut into more, shorter rows that fit across the screen; at the usual sizes nothing changes.
- **Leaving the settings search with the keyboard.** In the settings, Enter, Tab or Down in the search box now go to the first setting found. Before, they carried on from wherever the keyboard was before the search: from **Done** round to the **Lyrics** switch (so Space then turned the lyrics off), from **Reset all** to **Done**, and from a setting that was also found to the one after it, skipping the first results.
- **Ctrl+Tab back to a tab with the Narrator.** In the settings, when Ctrl+Tab brings you back to a tab where the setting you were on has been hidden in the meantime (like **Depth** after you switch the layout away from Arc, or after picking a look), the keyboard goes to the next setting that shows and the Narrator names that one. Before, the Narrator read out the hidden setting, while Left, Right and Space then changed the setting after it.
- **Preview with the Narrator.** In the settings, the Narrator now reads what the preview shows when you press **Preview** ("Previewing. Click or press any key to go back.", or that nothing is playing and how to start the demo song), and names the **Preview** button again when you come back. Before, it said nothing at either step, so there was no telling that the settings had gone or how to get them back.
- **Where a setting sits, with the Narrator.** In the settings, when the keyboard moves onto a setting, the Narrator now also says where it sits among the settings that show on that tab (or in the search results), in Minecraft's own words ("Selected list row 3 out of 12"), as the game's own lists do. Hidden settings aren't counted, and changing the setting after that says just its new value, without the place again.
- **A setting that disappears under the keyboard.** In the settings, when the setting the keyboard is on disappears (like **This song** when the song stops, or the Spotify sign-in problem once you are signed in), the keyboard now goes to the next setting that shows, and the Narrator names it. Before, the keyboard moved on without a word, and from the last setting of a tab (like that Spotify problem) it went on to **Reset all**.
- **Esc in the settings search with the Narrator.** In the settings, Esc in the search box (or in its results) now has the Narrator say "Search cleared" and where the keyboard is now: the setting it is on, or the tab. Before, it said nothing, so there was no telling that the settings were still open, and pressing Esc again to check closed them.
- **One focus ring while typing a settings search.** In the settings, while you type in the search box, only the search box looks focused. Before, the white ring also stayed on the setting or button the keyboard was on before (like **Done**), so two things looked focused at once.
- **Song places with the Narrator.** In the song library, the Narrator now says where a song is in the whole list ("50 of 300") and how many songs a search found in all. Before, it counted only the songs loaded so far: the 50th of 300 liked songs was "50 of 50", as if the list ended there, and a search that found hundreds said "10 results".
- **Esc in a playlist from the view buttons.** In the song library, pressing Esc while the keyboard is on the grid, shelf or carousel button inside an open playlist now closes the playlist and puts the keyboard back on that playlist, and the Narrator names it. Before, the keyboard stayed on the button and the Narrator said nothing.
- **Song library messages with the Narrator.** In the song library, the Narrator now reads every message as it shows, also one with the same words as the one before. Before, pressing Enter on the next made-up song said nothing (its "These songs are made up, so nothing plays" was the same as the last song's), and neither did a song that failed to start for the same reason as the one before.
- **Constellations on the Synthwave and Moonlight skies.** On the **Synthwave** and **Moonlight** night skies, the constellations' lines now show whenever the sky does. Before, they vanished at dusk and dawn, while rain dimmed the sky, and with a low sky **Strength** (below about 18% they never showed), leaving only the constellations' stars. Turning **Constellations** on or off there now fades them smoothly into the sky instead of a jump part of the way through.
- **Lyrics behind the Synthwave and Moonlight skies.** With **See through blocks** off (or **Draw on top** on Never) and the lyrics in the sky, the **Synthwave** and **Moonlight** skies no longer cover them at a low render distance (or a server's low view distance): at 5 or less the sun, its glow and the ends of the rows hid them, and at 2 the whole sky did. A big **Distance** did the same at the usual render distances. The lyrics now come near enough to stay in front of the sky; they look the same size, and at the default Distance nothing changes from render distance 9 up.
- **Clouds over the Synthwave and Moonlight skies.** Minecraft's clouds now show over the whole **Synthwave** and **Moonlight** skies, as they already did on 26.3. Before (1.21.1 to 26.2), the sky hid every cloud beyond it, so the clouds stopped in a hard circle high up (about 55 degrees up at render distance 12), and at render distance 6 or less no clouds showed at all. With a shader pack on, nothing changes.
- **Clouds and lyrics behind the night skies (26.2 and 26.3).** On Minecraft 26.2 and 26.3, Minecraft's clouds now show over the **Aurora**, **Nebula**, **Eclipse**, **Galaxy** and **Comet** skies, the sparkles and the shooting stars, as on the other versions. Before, every cloud behind one of the sky's shapes was hidden, so the clouds stopped in the shape of the aurora's curtains, the nebula's clouds or the eclipse's glow and milky way, even with the default **Aurora**. With **See through blocks** off (or **Draw on top** on Never), the lyrics in the sky also lost every letter a curtain, a nebula cloud, a sparkle or a shooting star crossed: at render distance 11 or less at the default **Distance**, and at any render distance with a big Distance. With a shader pack on, nothing changes.
- **Clouds in front of the eclipse.** With the **Eclipse** sky, a cloud passing in front of the black sun now covers it, as it covers the glow round it. Before (1.21.1 to 26.2), the black disc stayed on top of every cloud in front of it. With a shader pack on, nothing changes.
- **Shooting stars over the eclipse.** With the **Eclipse** sky, shooting stars and sparkles now always show over the black sun. Before (1.21.10 and newer), in about half of the game starts the black disc covered them where they crossed it, and on 26.2 and 26.3 they cut holes in it instead.
- **"Loading" with the Narrator.** In the song library, the Narrator now says "Loading" only while songs are really on their way, and once they are there it says how many the list has ("300 songs", "6 playlists"). Before, it said "Loading" when the library opened even for the made-up songs and **Recently heard**, which are there at once, and it said nothing when a list finished loading, so you could not tell it was ready.
- **Trying more songs again with the keyboard.** In the song library, when the next songs of a long list fail to load and the automatic tries are over, the keyboard can now try again: Down from the grid's last row (Right from the shelf's last column) reaches the line that says why, and Enter or Space there tries again. The Narrator reads that line with its **Try again** button, says "Loading", and then the first new song, or why it failed again. Before, only a click on that line tried again.
- **Arabic song names in the top bar and on the Record card.** An Arabic or Persian song title or artist no longer leaves a wide empty gap before the "·" and the artist in the top bar, no longer makes the bar wider than its text, and is no longer cut short with "…" where it fits. On the **Record card**, an Arabic lyric line sits in the middle of its strip, and one that fits shows whole instead of sliding with its end cut off.
- **Emoji in song names.** A song title, artist or album with an emoji like ❤️ or ☀️ no longer shows a dashed box with "VS16" in it after the emoji, in the top bar, on the **Record card** or wherever else SkyLyrics shows the song. A hidden word joiner, zero-width space or byte order mark in a song name no longer draws as a box either.
- **Film and session songs in a browser.** With Spotify's Web Player (or another music site) in a browser, a song named like "Song - From "Film"", "Song - From the Film Soundtrack", "Song - Recorded at …" or "Song - Bonus Track" is no longer split into the song's name as the artist and the tag as the title: the top bar and the **Record card** show the real artist, and the lyrics are looked up for the right song.
- **Emoji in lyrics.** A lyric line with an emoji like ❤️ or ✨️ no longer shows a dashed box with "VS16" in it after the emoji, in the sky (**Lines**, **Arc** and **World**), in the top bar's lyric line or on the **Record card**.
- **Arabic lyrics in the Lines layout.** An Arabic or Persian lyric line that fits across the sky now stays on one row instead of breaking in two, and a long one takes only the rows it needs (two where it took three) instead of short rows with room to spare. The same goes for the lyrics on the title screen.

### Faster

- **No hitch when a setting changes.** Settings are saved in the background, so pressing a timing key or closing the settings no longer makes the game pause for a moment while the file is written (most noticeable on Windows when an antivirus or OneDrive holds the file). A change made right before you quit is still saved.
- **Smaller saved album covers.** Album covers are saved as small 128-pixel pictures, so they load faster and take less disk space, and they are made in memory instead of through a temporary file. Big album covers saved by an older version are made small the next time they show, so an old cover folder shrinks as you play those songs again.
- **Lighter in the background.** On a Mac, while the lyrics are switched off and no SkyLyrics screen is open, the mod checks Spotify or Music about every 15 seconds instead of every second; it checks at once when you switch the lyrics back on. On Windows, while the lyrics are switched off and no SkyLyrics screen is open, the mod asks Windows for the song about every 15 seconds instead of every half second; it asks at once when you switch the lyrics back on.
- **Long lines in World, sparkles, faint glow.** A long line in the World layout (a fast rap verse) is measured once when it starts instead of once per letter, which could stall that frame. Sparkles that are out of view are no longer drawn, and a faint glow in the Arc layout uses the same lighter drawing the Lines layout already did.
- **Lighter lyrics and sky effects.** Lines and Arc lyrics and the Galaxy sky do less work each frame. The default Aurora sky, the Nebula clouds and stars, and the constellations skip the parts behind you or off the side of the screen. They look the same and cost less each frame. While the day goes by, the stars' brightness is worked out once a frame instead of twice. The Moonlight clouds, the Comet streamers and the eclipse corona do less work each frame.
- **Lighter bars, menus and cards.** The bar keeps its line laid out instead of measuring it again every frame, and the card keeps its times and cut titles. Nothing looks different. The settings window lays out each row once per frame instead of several times, and remembers the right-to-left text it has already put in order. Nothing looks different. A card without a cover works out its big letter once instead of every frame, and a title that starts with a letter piled with accents shows just the letter. Names cut short with "…" in the song library and the settings are cut once instead of every frame.
- **Less garbage each frame.** The World and Arc lyrics and the font checks make fewer throwaway objects each frame, so Java has less to clean up. Nothing looks different.

### Changed

- **Which lyrics are used.** The mod is stricter about which lyrics it shows and rechecks saved ones.
  - When the lyrics site (LRCLIB) doesn't have the song, the mod no longer shows lyrics from a different song, even one by the same artist, so such a song now shows none. A title with a translation or romanisation in brackets still finds its lyrics.
  - A copy of the lyrics whose song length is more than 20 seconds off your song's is no longer used (it was often another version's lyrics).
  - When the lyrics site's best match for a song has only plain lyrics, the mod also looks for a synced copy before settling for the plain one. A lyrics file with only tags and no lines no longer counts as an answer.
  - Lyrics saved by version 0.8.0 or older are checked again the next time you play the song. If the lyrics site has other lyrics for it, they replace the saved ones. If it has none, the saved ones stay for that play and are looked up fresh the next time.
- **Pauses and fades.** A line that is only "(Instrumental)", "(music)", "Instrumental", "♪ instrumental ♪", "(Intro)", "(Outro)", "(Solo)" or a note emoji now counts as a pause instead of being shown as words. A line that is just "Music" is still sung. A line starting with a part tag such as "[Chorus] words" no longer shows the tag. In Lines and Arc, a line that ended more than a second and a half ago (the last lyric during the outro, or a line before a long instrumental part) fades out.
- **At most three flashes a second.** When lines come very quickly, the glow, crosshair, hat and sky flashes no longer restart for every line: they start at most three times a second. Normal songs look the same.
- **Themes keep your other settings.** Picking a theme now changes only what themes set (the layout, colours, fonts, glow, size, opacity, animation, sky and a few more). Settings no theme touches, such as **Karaoke fill**, **Shadow** and **Two-tone**, stay as you set them, and the theme still shows as picked (not Custom).
- **Floating distance.** With Floating placement, every step of the **Distance** slider now moves the lyrics nearer or farther (before, 8 to 24 were all the same distance, and so were 96 to 160). They keep the same size on screen, so you see it as you walk past them or with **See through blocks** off. The default is unchanged. With Floating placement, the **Distance** number now changes on every step of the slider; far out it used to stay the same while the lyrics still moved.
- **Timing sliders.** The **Timing** and **This song** sliders now reach 5 seconds either way.
  - A **This song** timing you set in version 0.8.0 for a video playing in a web browser, whose title ends in an extra tag such as "| Official Music Video", may need setting again once: such titles are now tidied before they are matched, so the old saved timing no longer finds the song.
- **Spotify asks less.** With Spotify signed in, when the lyrics are off and none of the mod's screens is open, the mod asks Spotify for the song only every 15 seconds. When Spotify keeps failing, the mod waits longer each time before asking again, but no longer than 30 seconds (a Spotify app that doesn't know your account waits a minute). When Spotify says it is busy, the mod waits as long as Spotify asks (up to 5 minutes).
- **Clearer messages.** With no Client ID pasted, the Music tab now says "Paste your Client ID first" and no "can't read your music player" pop-up appears. The old "Spotify sign-in needs port" line goes away when you press **Sign in** or **Sign out**. A bad connection while signing in or loading the song library says "Can't reach the internet or Spotify" instead of a raw error. The sign-in page opened in your browser reads right to left for Hebrew. A lyrics site that answers with an odd error shows "no lyrics" instead of blaming your internet. On a Mac, the "Nothing playing" bar in the settings no longer suggests browsers, and it stays quiet while the music player can't be read.
- **Settings texts and visibility.** Settings show only where they matter, and their texts say what they do.
  - The **Hide lyrics** card is now **Hide**, because its rows also hide the top bar, the **Record card** and the sky effects. The texts of **Karaoke fill** (it lights up the top bar's words too), **Top bar**, **Accent colour**, **Draw on top**, **Song name only on change**, **Hide in multiplayer**, **Show underground too** and **This song** now say what the setting really does. **Show underground too** only shows when **See through blocks** is off, since otherwise it changes nothing. **Karaoke fill** also shows in World while the top bar shows lyrics. **Depth** only shows in Arc, the one layout that draws it, and **Shadow** is hidden in Arc while **Depth** is on, since Depth replaces it there. The settings window's footer says just "Esc to close" when **Open settings** has no key, and the **Show or hide lyrics** key now says "Lyrics on" or "Lyrics off" above the hotbar. In a small window, the choices in a row of buttons (like the **Record card**'s corner) keep a gap between names instead of touching.
  - In the World layout, the settings it doesn't use (**Draw on top**, **Depth**, **Shadow**, **Pulse**, **Karaoke fill** and **Bigger current word**) are hidden, as **Animation** already was. With Floating placement, **Distance** shows the real distance in blocks (for example "10.7 blocks" rather than "64 blocks"). **Strength** now shows when only **Constellations** is on, since it changes how bright they are, and **Sky speed** and **Pulse with the lyrics** show with **Constellations** and the other sky effects too. **Background** (how dark the bar is) also shows when only the Record card is on, since the card uses it.
  - The **Height** setting is hidden for Arc when it has no effect (Floating, or Direction Follow), but still found by search. Changing Direction, Placement, Height or the view lock moves the Arc lines that use them right away instead of from the next line.
  - A sky **Strength** of 0 in the settings file now shows as 10%, where the slider starts. Settings search also finds English words in a Hebrew game, and pasted search text is cleaned up like typed text. A few English and Hebrew texts say what they mean (the previous line, **Preview**, **Aurora**).
  - The album picture is called "album cover" everywhere in the settings and help pages.
- **Reset all.** **Reset all** keeps your intro tour done, your update choice, your Spotify Client ID, your per-song timings and your recent searches.
- **Welcome tour and Hebrew texts.** The tour says which apps SkyLyrics can read on a Mac (Music and Spotify, not browsers), that macOS will ask for permission, and that signing in to Spotify is optional and needs Premium and a free developer app. On a Mac, the permission texts say "your launcher". The Music tab says "No Spotify or Music playing". The Hebrew texts speak in the plural, write Spotify and Minecraft in Hebrew letters, and say "no access" for the internet error. A few smoother lines (Draw on top, Karaoke fill, the Mac browser note).
- **Help pages.** The Troubleshooting page and FAQ now say what to expect with Replay Mod and Flashback recordings (the lyrics follow the music playing when you render, not when you recorded) and with Distant Horizons (which night skies can show in front of far-away terrain).
- **Game log.** The mod's lines in the game log no longer show song names or your home folder name, and a problem that repeats (offline, a failed save) is written once, so the log is safe to attach to a bug report.

- **World layout and seeking.** Jumping back a moment with the mod's progress bar (half a second is enough) now takes the World layout's words back too, and the line being sung places its words again from the new spot. A jump back made in the music player itself counts from 1.5 seconds as before, so a player that reports its position a little late never wipes the words in the middle of a song.
